jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
WHO WE ARE

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

BY JOINING OUR TEAM YOU’LL GET TO

  • Build the machine that builds the machine. Join TechOps at the forefront of advanced manufacturing, we’re building the production system that will enable commercial fusion. The Production lines, tooling, and processes are being developed from the ground up; you'll create the ways of working, not inherit them.

  • Work at the frontier of manufacturing technology. Bring your creativity to evaluate, qualify, and deploy processes with no industry playbook, every component you build and every process you shape goes directly into the core of the stellarator magnet technology.

  • Do work that matters, and see it grow. The hardware you build is the product and your career grows with it, from prototyping and process development through quality and industrialization, alongside exceptional colleagues from around the world.

  • Make an impact you can point to. In a small, fast-moving team, your calls on equipment, quality, and process directly shape how a world-class deep-tech company produces superconducting magnets with results visible on the shop floor, not buried in a slidedeck.

YOUR IMPACT

Develop and industrialize the manufacturing processes used to build HTS magnet coils.

Translate magnet designs into repeatable, high-yield production processes in collaboration with design, physics, and production teams.

Own the tooling, fixtures, and quality systems required to deliver consistent and reliable manufacturing outcomes.

Lead process development from prototype builds through the transition to full-scale manufacturing.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

  • Develop, qualify, and continuously improve manufacturing processes for HTS coil winding, insulation, impregnation, and joining, working closely with magnet design and materials engineers.

  • Drive design-for-manufacturing/design-for-assembly (DFM (Design for Manufacturing)/DFA (Design for Assembly)) collaboration with the design team, acting as the manufacturing voice in design reviews to keep coil designs buildable, scalable, and serviceable.

  • Design, procure, and validate tooling, fixtures, and jigs for precision winding and assembly of non-planar coil geometries, including capability studies where needed.

  • Define assembly sequences, work instructions, SOPs (Standard Operating Procedures), and visual aids for technicians, and maintain this documentation as designs evolve.

  • Define and implement process controls and inspection methods (dimensional, electrical, structural) to catch defects early and protect conductor integrity.

  • Lead NPI (New Product Introduction) campaigns, process trials and pilot builds, and provide hands-on floor support during prototype and early production builds.

  • Lead root-cause analysis and corrective actions (8D (Eight Disciplines problem-solving methodology), 5-Why, fishbone, etc.) for yield, quality, and cycle-time issues, and apply Lean/Six Sigma principles to drive measurable process improvement.

  • Support supplier qualification and incoming inspection criteria for tooling, components, and outsourced subassemblies.

  • Manage engineering/process change control as designs and processes mature.

  • Collaborate cross-functionally with design, quality, supply chain, and test engineering to resolve manufacturability issues early and support the ramp from prototype to serial production.

WHO YOU ARE

  • 3+ years specifying, procuring, installing, commissioning, and qualifying production equipment and/or automation for component manufacturing lines and/or assembly cells — including RFQ (Request for Quote) ownership, supplier management, FAT (Factory Acceptance Test)/SAT (Site Acceptance Test), and production ramp.

  • Hands-on experience designing tooling and fixtures for low-volume, high-precision production, and proficiency in CAD (Computer-Aided Design) (SolidWorks, CATIA, or similar) plus a solid grasp of GD&T (Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing).

  • Track record of writing clear work instructions, SOPs, and process documentation in a production or NPI(New Product Introduction) environment.

  • Working knowledge of process control, statistical methods, and structured root-cause problem solving (SPC (Statistical Process Control), FMEA (Failure Mode and Effects Analysis), 8D).

  • Experience supporting prototype or first-article builds directly on the floor, not just from a desk.

  • Strong communication skills in German or English.

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Materials Science, or a related field.

Nice to have:

  • Experience with Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) systems for engineering change control and manufacturing documentation management (e.g. Arena, Enovia).

  • Experience with Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES)/Platforms (e.g. Tulip, Delmia).

  • Experience working in a research-to-product transition environment, where designs and processes evolve rapidly.

  • Experience scaling a process from prototype to serial production in a startup or fast-moving environment.

INTERVIEW PROCESS

  • Recruiter Interview (30-60 min)

  • Technical Screening (30 min)

  • Technical Panel (3x60 min)

  • CEO call (30 min)

  • Do work that matters, and see it grow. The hardware you build is the product and your career grows with it, from prototyping and process development through quality and industrialization, alongside exceptional colleagues from around the world.

  • Make an impact you can point to. In a small, fast-moving team, your calls on equipment, quality, and process directly shape how a world-class deep-tech company produces superconducting magnets with results visible on the shop floor, not buried in a slidedeck.

YOUR IMPACT

Build and maintain medium- to long-term production plans that align engineering, procurement, and manufacturing.

Balance capacity, material availability, and evolving engineering requirements to enable predictable execution.

Identify and resolve constraints before they affect day-to-day production on the manufacturing floor.

Support the successful delivery of critical fusion hardware while improving efficiency, coordination, and transparency across manufacturing operations.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

  • Translate project milestones into detailed, resourced and executable manufacturing plans.

  • Perform capacity planning and balance workloads across internal and external manufacturing resources.

  • Coordinate with the Procurement & Logistics Department to optimize inventory availability, minimize shortages and support efficient material flow across manufacturing.

  • Anticipate the impact of evolving engineering requirements and material constraints on the production plan and adjust proactively ahead of execution.

  • Work closely with Manufacturing Engineering to incorporate process changes into production plans.

  • Partner with Program Managers to align production priorities with program objectives.

  • Analyze production performance data to identify risks to material availability, capacity and delivery timelines, feeding findings back into the plan.

  • Monitor planning-level metrics such as capacity utilization and lead times and use them to continuously improve the accuracy of the production plan.

  • Support the design, implementation and continuous improvement of production planning systems and processes, contributing to the selection and deployment of future ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning)/MRP (Material Requirements Planning) capabilities.

  • Contribute to the development of scalable production planning processes as Proxima transitions from prototype manufacturing to industrial deployment.

WHO YOU ARE

  • You have a degree in Industrial Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Operations Management or a related field, or equivalent practical experience in production planning, manufacturing operations or supply chain within a complex engineering environment (aerospace, fusion, automotive, energy or other high-tech manufacturing industries).

  • You have experience with production planning systems, MRP/ERP workflows and manufacturing data management and are excited by the opportunity to help implement and shape planning tools in a rapidly growing manufacturing organization.

  • You think in terms of capacity, material flow and constraints and you are comfortable modeling trade-offs before they become execution problems.

  • You thrive in fast-paced, dynamic environments where priorities evolve quickly and planning decisions have a direct impact on manufacturing execution.

  • You communicate effectively across multidisciplinary teams and can balance competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.

  • You are proactive, detail-oriented and comfortable working in an evolving hardware development environment.

INTERVIEW PROCESS

  • Recruiter Interview (30-60 min)

  • Technical Screening (30 min)

  • Technical Panel (3x60 min)

jobs.descriptionHtml:
WHO WE ARE

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

 

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

 

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

 

BY JOINING OUR TEAM YOU’LL GET TO

  • Build the machine that builds the machine. Join TechOps at the forefront of advanced manufacturing, we’re building the production system that will enable commercial fusion. The Production lines, tooling, and processes are being developed from the ground up; you'll create the ways of working, not inherit them.

  • Work at the frontier of manufacturing technology. Bring your creativity to evaluate, qualify, and deploy processes with no industry playbook, every component you build and every process you shape goes directly into the core of the stellarator magnet technology.

  • Do work that matters, and see it grow. The hardware you build is the product and your career grows with it, from prototyping and process development through quality and industrialization, alongside exceptional colleagues from around the world.

  • Make an impact you can point to. In a small, fast-moving team, your calls on equipment, quality, and process directly shape how a world-class deep-tech company produces superconducting magnets with results visible on the shop floor, not buried in a slidedeck.

YOUR IMPACT

Own the controls engineering for new magnet factory equipment supporting coil winding, impregnation, joining, and end-of-line testing.

Architect control systems and develop PLC (Programmable Logic Controller) software, primarily on Beckhoff platforms.

Commission and validate manufacturing equipment to ensure safe, reliable, and predictable operation.

Partner with mechanical, process, and manufacturing engineers to translate production requirements into robust, well-documented automation solutions.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

  • Participate in initial equipment conceptual development for new magnet manufacturing cells, balancing process requirements, layout, cost, and lead time.

  • Architect control system architecture and electrical schematics for new equipment, including sensor/actuator selection and panel layout coordination with electrical designers.

  • Write, debug, and maintain PLC programs (Structured Text, IEC (International Electrotechnical Commission) 61131-3) on Beckhoff TwinCAT, with an emphasis on code that's organized, documented, and reusable.

  • Specify and implement field network topology (e.g., EtherCAT, Profinet, EtherNet/IP, OPC-UA (Open Platform Communications Unified Architecture)) connecting equipment, sensors, and upstream/downstream systems.

  • Set up and tune servo drives and VFDs (Variable Frequency Drives) for precision motion control on winding, handling, and assembly equipment.

  • Design intuitive HMI (Human-Machine Interface)/SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) screens for operator use and troubleshooting.

  • Commission new equipment end-to-end: FAT (Factory Acceptance Test)/SAT (Site Acceptance Test), installation, integration, and initial process validation.

  • Use hand tools and diagnostic instruments (multimeters, oscilloscopes, etc.) for hands-on electrical troubleshooting during build and commissioning.

  • Implement control-reliable safety systems in line with relevant machine safety and electrical standards.

  • Document control architecture, code, and equipment operation to support handover and future sustaining work.

  • Collaborate with manufacturing, mechanical, and process engineers to ensure controls solutions match the realities of magnet coil production.

WHO YOU ARE

  • In-depth knowledge of Beckhoff controls systems (TwinCAT 3).

  • Good Structured Text (IEC 61131-3) programming skills.

  • Able to use common hand tools and diagnostic instruments such as multimeters.

  • Proficiency in field network topology, both theory and practical applications.

  • 2–5 years of experience in controls engineering for manufacturing or automation equipment, ideally on electromechanical or precision systems.

  • Experience commissioning servo drives/VFDs and integrating sensors, actuators, and safety devices.

  • Familiarity with HMI/SCADA platforms (TwinCAT HMI, WinCC, Ignition, or similar).

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

Nice to have:

  • Experience with CAD (Computer-Aided Design) electrical drafting tools (e.g., AutoCAD Electrical, EPLAN).

  • Scripting experience (Python, SQL) for data acquisition or MES (Manufacturing Execution System)/database integration.

  • Machine vision experience.

  • Greenfield or startup equipment commissioning experience.

  • Working knowledge of relevant electrical and machine safety standards (e.g., EN (European Norm) 60204-1, IEC 61439, ISO (International Organization for Standardization) 13849).

INTERVIEW PROCESS

  • Recruiter Interview (30-60 min)

  • Technical Screening (30 min)

  • Technical Panel (3x60 min)

  • CEO call (30 min)

WHY JOIN PROXIMA FUSION

  • You will get to work on some of the most complex tech challenges to bring abundant, safe, clean energy to the world.

  • You'll get to join and learn from an exceptional selection of accomplished and driven individuals.

  • Do your life’s best work and enjoy the journey.

  • Get to show that big things are possible in Europe when you assemble the best talent.

YOUR IMPACT

You will support the industrialisation of production processes for magnet production, contributing directly to the execution of key activities within Proxima’s magnet program.

You will play a central role in designing, programming and operating automation cells performing a wide array of production processes such as welding, bonding, sealing and coating.

You will operate across a wide range of technical tasks, from design and engineering to hands on production work, and collaborating closely with engineers and technicians

WHAT YOU WILL DO

  • Advise on future line design and automation concepts

  • Define the requirements for automation cells for different processes to ensure performance, repeatability and safe operation

  • Contribute to the development of control strategies for new production lines

  • You will build and commission automation cells, including running FAT at supplier sites

  • Identify and test different manufacturing and in-process monitoring approaches

  • Design jigs and tools for magnet industrialised production

  • Support in the process development and prototyping of magnets, with scalability and repeatability in mind.

  • Collaborate closely with engineers and technicians across multiple teams

WHO YOU ARE

  • A master´s degree in mechanical, mechatronics or similar engineering field

  • A wide experience in robotics, automation and process monitoring in an industrial setting

  • Strong hands-on experience in production environments over a wide range of production processes (for ex. welding, machining, assembly, bonding)

  • Experience with robotic simulation and offline programming (e.g. RoboGuide, RobotStudio, Process Simulate). Previous work on FANUC systems is a plus

  • Familiarity with industrial communication protocols (e.g., OPC UA, Ethernet, Profinet)

  • Proficient in industrial-level PLC programming

  • Ability to work across a variety of tasks in a dynamic environment

  • Reliable, proactive, and solution-oriented mindset

  • Strong team player, able to collaborate closely with engineers and technical staff

  • A high performer who loves challenges and is not afraid to experiment, take risks and learn from mistakes.

NICE TO HAVE

  • Familiarity in both prototype manufacturing and industrial manufacturing

  • Proficiency in CAD: good knowledge of Catia V5 or 3DExperience are considered as a plus

  • Exposure to SCADA systems or MES integration

  • Familiarity with Beckhoff PLC and motion control

  • Knowledge of safety standards and risk assessments in automated environments

jobs.title: Microwave Design Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
WHO WE ARE

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

 

WHY JOIN PROXIMA FUSION

  • Work on a civilisation-scale problem - Clean, baseload fusion energy is one of the few genuinely world-changing challenges, and every hire in Finance, People, or Legal directly accelerates the path to a working stellarator.

  • Grow as fast as the company does - With headcount set to roughly 5x in a few years and major technical milestones ahead on the path to our demo machine and first power plant, your role grows under you; today's hire is tomorrow's function lead.

  • Tackle problems that don't exist elsewhere - Fusion sits at a rare intersection of deep-tech R&D, industrial procurement, government relations, and venture financing, so non-tech functions face challenges no other workplace can offer.

YOUR IMPACT

As a microwave design engineer, you will help build the basis for the millimeter wave hardware acting as the spark plug that initiates a fusion plasma and raises its temperature to greater than 100 million degrees. You’ll join the Alpha Heating System team ready to drive the integrated RF and thermo-mechanical design of high-power components, and help build and test these components in the lab before installing them at scale on our net scientific gain Alpha stellarator.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

  • Provide innovative solutions to complex RF engineering challenges by collaborating closely with physicists to ensure component designs meet the Alpha plasma physics and thermal-mechanical constraints.

  • Develop designs and evaluate vendor designs to determine an optimal path to efficiently deliver our power to the stellarator - driving down the denominator of input power that will limit fusion power plant gain Q=Pout/Pin - and drive down costs.

  • Draw from and contribute to our stellarator development process, interfacing your RF components with other stellarator systems.

  • Contribute to mechanical and thermal analysis and sensitivity studies for component viability under the loads and stresses imposed by the combination of vacuum, magnetic fields, temperatures, and MW-scale RF loads.

  • Interface with the Alpha project management teams to realize the delivery of RF components and meet the tight Proxima timelines.

WHO YOU ARE

  • A highly capable RF engineer with experience in millimeter waves and knowledge of the tools and best practices for design of these systems

  • Demonstrated familiarly with RF modeling codes - SURF3D, CST, COMSOL, GdfidL, openEMS, even self-developed python codes or ones plasma physics community hasn’t heard of - capable of performing modeling at 200 GHz frequencies

  • Experience validating first-of-a-kind designs with uncertain performance, working as part of a team on multi-scale and multi-physics simulations, testing, and prototyping.

  • Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to articulate complex technical concepts clearly and persuasively.

  • Experience with gyrotrons and associated components - transmission systems, launcher antennas, rf loads; experience with plasma physics is a plus.

  • Understanding of quasi optical propagation of millimeter waves; ray tracing and where it breaks down

INTERVIEW PROCESS

  • Recruiter Interview (30-60 min)

  • Technical Screening (30 min)

  • Technical Panel (3x60 min)

  • You will get to work on some of the most complex tech challenges to bring abundant, safe, clean energy to the world

  • You'll get to join and learn from an exceptional selection of accomplished and driven individuals

  • Do your life’s best work and enjoy the journey

  • Get to show that big things are possible in Europe when you assemble the best talent

YOUR IMPACT

  • Shape the future of Proxima’s simulation platform: we design and develop the platform; stellarator researchers and engineers use it to mature the design of Alpha and Stellaris; you will imagine and build with us novel solutions for simulation tools that spark joy and reduce time-to-insight

  • Accelerate Stellarator R&D, at the company at its forefront: we work side by side with researchers and engineers to ensure what we build immediately boosts the speed Proxima Fusion’s Stellarator design program

WHAT YOU WILL DO

You will join the Simulation Platform Team, a software platform team that balances development of core products with direct support to researchers, adapting to the Stellarator design program’s strategy and priorities. In your first six months you will e.g. add features to our in-house simulation pipeline automation system and ensure that AI agents can work with it efficiently.

  • On the platform engineering side you will design, develop and maintain next-generation software solutions for stellarator simulation and design, targeted to human and agentic use; for example:

    • Python libraries enabling automation of large-scale simulation workflows

    • cloud-based data storage that keeps everyone in sync

    • web applications that foster cross-domain collaboration and knowledge discovery

    • integration of AI tools where they actually provide leverage

WHO WE ARE

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

TEAM AND ROLE

  • Shape the architecture of the world’s first commercial fusion power plant – Own system-level decisions that determine how a first-of-a-kind energy technology is designed, integrated, and ultimately deployed at scale.

  • Solve some of the most complex engineering challenges in industry – Work across tightly coupled disciplines (plasma physics, magnets, cryogenics, manufacturing, controls, and more) to resolve critical trade-offs and turn cutting-edge science into a functioning product.

  • Build real hardware with a pragmatic, fast-moving team from all over the world – Combine advanced simulation and systems thinking with a strong execution mindset, focusing on practical engineering solutions that accelerate the path to commercial fusion energy.

WHY JOIN PROXIMA FUSION

  • You will get to work on some of the most complex tech challenges to bring abundant, safe, clean energy to the world.

  • You'll get to join and learn from an exceptional selection of accomplished and driven individuals.

  • Do your life’s best work and enjoy the journey.

  • Get to show that big things are possible in Europe when you assemble the best talent.

YOUR IMPACT

As Lead R&D Engineer for the Stellaris tritium-breeding blanket, you will build and lead Proxima Fusion’s blanket development from initial concept to first prototype tests. You will translate a defined R&D budget into a small set of parallel breeder-blanket concepts, developed rapidly with external research and industrial partners.

Remote maintainability is a fundamental part of the blanket architecture from day one. Each concept must be thought with the power plant architecture in mind and demonstrate how blanket modules can be installed, connected, inspected, replaced and recovered remotely.

The objective is to leverage existing public research, challenge the most consequential assumptions, learn from hardware quickly and iterate to a functional blanket concept for our future commercial plant fleet.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

  • Own the blanket design from initial requirements through conceptual design, prototype manufacture and testing, with accountability for budget, schedule and technical outcomes.

  • Own the integrated remote-maintenance architecture for each concept, including segmentation, access, handling, service connections, inspection, replacement and recovery from failed operations.

  • Own the compliance analysis across neutronics, thermal hydraulics, structural integrity, materials, tritium, decommissioning, safety and remote maintenance.

  • Own the rapid fail-fast prototype: select what to test and lead its design, procurement, manufacture, instrumentation, commissioning and test campaign on ambitious timelines.

  • Own the translation of test results into updated models, requirements, risk assessments and design decisions.

  • Own and build the multidisciplinary, technical design team.

WHO YOU ARE

  • A Master’s degree or higher in mechanical engineering, nuclear engineering, materials science, chemical engineering, physics or equivalent experience.

  • Have led the development of complex nuclear, thermal, chemical or energy technology from conceptual design into hardware and testing, under budget and time constraints.

  • Able to lead multidisciplinary trade studies without converging prematurely on a preferred solution.

  • Strong knowledge in several relevant domains, such as thermal hydraulics, structural mechanics, neutronics, nuclear materials, tritium systems, high-temperature coolants, corrosion, manufacturing or remote handling.

  • Able to distinguish between analysis that enables a decision and analysis that merely adds detail.

  • Comfortable structuring and managing technical work with external institutes, industrial partners and specialist suppliers.

  • Willing to test critical assumptions early, learn from failure and stop weak development paths.

  • Able to make clear and defensible engineering decisions under uncertainty.

  • Experience with fusion blankets, fission-reactor components, breeder materials, tritium systems or remotely maintained nuclear equipment are an advantage, but are explicitly not necessary.

INTERVIEW PROCESS

  • Recruiter Interview (30-60 min)

  • Technical Screening (30 min)

  • Technical Panel (3x60 min)

WHO WE ARE

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

 

WHY JOIN PROXIMA FUSION

  • You will get to work on some of the most complex tech challenges to bring abundant, safe, clean energy to the world.

  • You'll get to join and learn from an exceptional selection of accomplished and driven individuals.

  • Do your life’s best work and enjoy the journey.

  • Get to show that big things are possible in Europe when you assemble the best talent.

 

YOUR IMPACT

At Proxima Fusion, we're developing the world's leading stellarator technology. To turn cutting-edge designs into reality, we need skilled technicians who can bring complex, first-of-a-kind hardware to life. As a Technician at Proxima Fusion, you'll work hands-on with Proxima-designed components, magnets, mechanical assemblies and other critical systems, supporting their build, assembly, integration and testing.

Working closely with Engineering, Manufacturing and Quality, you'll help turn ambitious designs into reliable hardware, solve practical challenges on the shop floor and contribute to developing the processes and tooling needed to build Alpha. This is a unique opportunity to work at the intersection of advanced engineering and hands-on manufacturing, helping build one of Europe's most ambitious engineering projects.

 

WHAT YOU WILL DO

  • Maintain, troubleshoot and repair machinery across our magnet factory,keeping equipment safe, accurate and available.

  • Carry out preventive maintenance, inspections and repairs on mechanical, electromechanical and pneumatic systems.

  • Diagnose breakdowns, intermittent faults and undocumented failures. Resolve the root cause and verify safe operation before returning equipment to service.

  • Assemble, install, align, and commission new equipment.

  • Support factory and site acceptance tests, installation checks.

  • Work with multiple teams to distinguish machine faults from setup, material, process or measurement problems.

  • Work with controls and manufacturing engineering to tune equipment, including winding tension, motion, vacuum and thermal profiles, within approved process limits.

  • Identify wear early, flag long-lead items and communicate to the lead technician.

  • Record failure modes, downtime, repairs, parts used and equipment modifications.

  • Apply lockout/tagout, safe isolation, stored-energy controls and controlled restart procedures.

  • Provide clear handovers on equipment condition, outstanding faults and any operating restrictions.

WHO YOU ARE

  • A technical apprenticeship or vocational qualification in industrial maintenance, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering or mechatronics, or equivalent hands-on experience.

  • Hands-on experience maintaining and repairing production or process equipment.

  • Strong electrical and mechanical diagnostic skills.

  • The ability to interpret engineering drawings, equipment manuals and electrical or pneumatic schematics, and practical familiarity with mechanisms, pneumatics, drives and sensors.

  • Confidence using workshop tools and measuring equipment to strip, rebuild, align and inspect machine components accurately.

  • A disciplined approach to electrical and machine safety, safe isolation and stored energy, with sound judgement about when specialist support is required.

  • The ability to organise assigned work independently, keep reliable records and adapt as equipment and processes develop.

  • Working English for understanding technical instructions, recording work and communicating with technicians, engineers and suppliers.

Nice to have

  • Experience with reel-to-reel machinery, tension control, precision motion, or cable and conductor handling.

  • Experience diagnosing programmable logic controller (PLC) systems beyond the operator screen, including Beckhoff/TwinCAT or comparable controls.

  • Experience commissioning custom machinery, a new cell or a new production line, including factory or site acceptance testing.

  • Hydraulic, vacuum, cryogenic or high-voltage equipment experience; an electrical qualification such as Elektrofachkraft.

  • Experience with computerised maintenance management systems (CMMS), establishing preventive-maintenance programmes or structured reliability improvement.

  • German language skills.

 

INTERVIEW PROCESS

  • Recruiter Interview (30-60 min)

  • Technical Screening (30 min)

  • Technical Panel (3x60 min)

  • CEO call (30 min)


This job would require frequent travels to our office in Villigen ( Zurich, CH)

  • Set up, operate and change over the HTS cable line and plate assembly stations. Deliver routine production alongside complex, first-article and non-standard builds.

  • Carry out precision assembly, fitting, fabrication and approved rework using drawings, work instructions and practical judgement.

  • Troubleshoot process, assembly and quality problems, including handling issues, setup errors, dimensional variation and inconsistent output. Contain affected work, investigate the cause and help implement a verified correction.

  • Resolve unfamiliar or undocumented scenarios within agreed safety, quality and change-control limits. Develop and document practical solutions, and obtain engineering or quality approval before proceeding outside your authority.

  • Verify setups and initial output, and inspect assemblies against released acceptance criteria at assigned in-process and final checks. Raise non-conformances and refer deviations or product-disposition decisions to the authorised owner.

  • Work with equipment technicians on machine faults; provide design and manufacturing engineers clear measurements and feedback on buildability, tooling, and process performance.

  • Run first-article builds and process trials with manufacturing engineering, and help prove tooling, fixtures and equipment ready for production.

  • Write, redline and improve work instructions and standard operating procedures using build experience. Route changes through review and release, and help improve cycle time, yield and repeatability.

  • Maintain complete build records, material traceability, deviation records and clear handovers.

     

WHO YOU ARE

  • Substantial hands-on experience building complex, high-precision assemblies, with capability beyond routine machine operation.

  • A technical apprenticeship or vocational qualification in a relevant discipline, or equivalent practical experience.

  • Confidence interpreting engineering drawings, assembly requirements and geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T), and using measuring equipment to verify work.

  • Proven practical troubleshooting skills, including experience investigating unfamiliar problems and distinguishing symptoms from underlying causes.

  • Experience setting up equipment, using fixtures and handling sensitive components or materials with consistent workmanship.

  • The judgement to work with incomplete instructions while recognising when to proceed, stop or escalate, supported by a practical understanding of traceability, non-conformance and change control.

  • The ability to write instructions others can follow, explain technical problems clearly and train or support less-experienced technicians.

  • Working English for drawings, procedures, technical discussions and production records.

Nice to have

  • Experience with winding, insulation, impregnation, soldering, brazing, precision bonding or reel-to-reel processing.

  • Experience introducing new products or processes, supporting pilot builds or transferring development work into production.

  • Familiarity with structured problem solving, such as Lean/Six Sigma improvement methods.

  • German language skills.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

  • Maintain, troubleshoot and repair machinery across our magnet factory,keeping equipment safe, accurate and available.

  • Carry out preventive maintenance, inspections and repairs on mechanical, electromechanical and pneumatic systems.

  • Diagnose breakdowns, intermittent faults and undocumented failures. Resolve the root cause and verify safe operation before returning equipment to service.

  • Assemble, install, align, and commission new equipment.

  • Support factory and site acceptance tests, installation checks.

  • Work with multiple teams to distinguish machine faults from setup, material, process or measurement problems.

  • Work with controls and manufacturing engineering to tune equipment, including winding tension, motion, vacuum and thermal profiles, within approved process limits.

  • Identify wear early, flag long-lead items and communicate to the lead technician.

  • Record failure modes, downtime, repairs, parts used and equipment modifications.

  • Apply lockout/tagout, safe isolation, stored-energy controls and controlled restart procedures.

  • Provide clear handovers on equipment condition, outstanding faults and any operating restrictions.

WHO YOU ARE

  • A technical apprenticeship or vocational qualification in industrial maintenance, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering or mechatronics, or equivalent hands-on experience.

  • Hands-on experience maintaining and repairing production or process equipment.

  • Strong electrical and mechanical diagnostic skills.

  • The ability to interpret engineering drawings, equipment manuals and electrical or pneumatic schematics, and practical familiarity with mechanisms, pneumatics, drives and sensors.

  • Confidence using workshop tools and measuring equipment to strip, rebuild, align and inspect machine components accurately.

  • A disciplined approach to electrical and machine safety, safe isolation and stored energy, with sound judgement about when specialist support is required.

  • The ability to organise assigned work independently, keep reliable records and adapt as equipment and processes develop.

  • Working English for understanding technical instructions, recording work and communicating with technicians, engineers and suppliers.

Nice to have

  • Experience diagnosing programmable logic controller (PLC) systems beyond the operator screen, including Beckhoff/TwinCAT or comparable controls.

  • Experience with reel-to-reel machinery, tension control, precision motion, or cable and conductor handling.

  • Experience commissioning custom machinery, a new cell or a new production line, including factory or site acceptance testing.

  • Hydraulic, vacuum, cryogenic or high-voltage equipment experience; an electrical qualification such as Elektrofachkraft.

  • Experience with computerised maintenance management systems (CMMS), establishing preventive-maintenance programmes or structured reliability improvement.

  • German language skills.

 

INTERVIEW PROCESS

  • Recruiter Interview (30-60 min)

  • Technical Screening (30 min)

  • Technical Panel (3x60 min)

  • CEO call (30 min)

Working closely with Engineering, Manufacturing and Quality, you'll help turn ambitious designs into reliable hardware, solve practical challenges on the shop floor and contribute to developing the processes and tooling needed to build Alpha. This is a unique opportunity to work at the intersection of advanced engineering and hands-on manufacturing, helping build one of Europe's most ambitious engineering projects.

 

WHAT YOU WILL DO

  • Build, assemble and modify prototypes, experimental hardware, custom tooling and development rigs for engineering and special projects across the programme.

  • Turn engineering drawings, models, and sketches into practical hardware. Clarify missing requirements and agree the build approach with the responsible engineer before committing to uncertain or irreversible steps.

  • Fabricate and adapt components using fitting, cutting, drilling, soldering, bonding and assembly techniques within your competence. Coordinate specialist machining, welding or other work when needed.

  • Identify buildability issues early, including tolerance stacks, inaccessible fasteners, component fit and assembly sequence, and provide practical feedback to the design team.

  • Prepare and run development trials, including winding, joining, insulation and impregnation trials as assigned. Install instrumentation, commission rigs with engineers, take measurements and record what changed and what happened.

  • Investigate unexpected behaviour, propose practical fixes and work through build-test-modify iterations with engineers.

  • Organise the practical delivery of assigned projects: source small parts and consumables through agreed purchasing routes, arrange tools and build activities, and keep the workshop ready for use. Communicate progress, blockers and changing priorities to the lead technician.

  • Keep clear as-built records, annotated drawings, photographs, settings and trial observations so another technician can reproduce the work and understand each modification.

  • Transfer proven prototypes and methods to manufacturing or routine testing through initial work instructions, tooling, assembly sequences, training and technical handovers.

  • Work with engineers to identify hazards and establish the necessary risk assessments and controls before starting work on unproven hardware.

     

WHO YOU ARE

  • A technical apprenticeship or vocational qualification in mechanical, electrical, mechatronic or related engineering work, or equivalent hands-on experience.

  • Hands-on experience building, modifying and troubleshooting mechanical or electromechanical hardware in a workshop, laboratory, development or advanced manufacturing environment.

  • The ability to interpret engineering drawings, tolerances and 3D models, with working familiarity with geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T) and practical measurement skills.

  • Confident hand-tool and workshop skills, sound fabrication and assembly judgement, and a willingness to develop unfamiliar techniques.

  • Resourcefulness with incomplete information: you investigate, ask useful questions, find suitable parts and propose a practical next step while keeping the engineering objective clear.

  • Sound judgement about technical uncertainty, safety and when a build or design change requires engineering review before proceeding.

  • The ability to organise work, adapt to agreed priority changes and document configurations and findings clearly.

  • Working English for technical discussions, drawings, instructions and build records.

Nice to have

  • Specialist fabrication skills such as manual or CNC machining, sheet-metal work, welding, brazing or additive manufacturing.

  • Experience creating or modifying simple parts and fixtures in CATIA, SolidWorks, Fusion 360 or similar CAD tools.

  • Experience with instrumentation, sensors, data acquisition, electrical wiring, vacuum, cryogenics or superconducting hardware.

  • Experience with composites, resins, vacuum bagging, insulation or impregnation.

  • Experience taking first-of-a-kind hardware or a prototype process through to repeatable manufacturing and technical handover.

  • German language skills.

 

INTERVIEW PROCESS

  • Recruiter Interview (30-60 min)

  • Technical Screening (30 min)

  • Technical Panel (3x60 min)

  • CEO call (30 min)

 

This job would require frequent travels to our office in Villigen ( Zurich, CH)

jobs.descriptionHtml:
WHO WE ARE

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

 

WHY JOIN PROXIMA FUSION

  • You will get to work on some of the most complex tech challenges to bring abundant, safe, clean energy to the world.

  • You'll get to join and learn from an exceptional selection of accomplished and driven individuals.

  • Do your life’s best work and enjoy the journey.

  • Get to show that big things are possible in Europe when you assemble the best talent.

 

YOUR IMPACT

Build and lead the team owning the architecture, design, and integration of the facility-wide monitoring and control systems for Alpha, Proxima’s net energy gain stellarator. We are moving away from legacy industrial control paradigms towards a fully integrated control and observability platform. We are looking for a leader inspired by the cutting edge of robotics, autonomous vehicles, and modern aerospace avionics to lead this development. Pushing forwards the cutting edge of control, data, and monitoring capabilities for energy infrastructure, your role will span physical infrastructure, systems programming, real-time operations and scalable facility compute.

 

WHAT YOU WILL DO

  • Specify mission control & supervisory software: Own the overarching supervisory control, telemetry pipelines, and live monitoring stack across Alpha and future Proxima facilities.

  • Build the facility data center & data platform: Design, deploy, and scale the facility compute hardware and software data platform responsible for high-speed ingestion, streaming telemetry, storage, and live visualization.

  • Drive functional safety strategy: Define the device-wide technical strategy for functional safety, collaborating directly with internal engineers and external regulatory stakeholders.

  • Lead physical facility & environmental integration: Partner with facility teams to ensure physical services, cabling, and infrastructure support the I&C architecture under harsh radiation and magnetic field constraints.

  • Drive hardware R&D: Identify R&D opportunities for control and automation hardware. Act as an expert customer to specify and co-design with external vendors.

  • Standardize clean interface boundaries: Establish hardware and software interface standards across subsystems. Collaborate closely with system teams that own edge-level hardware and software.

     

WHO YOU ARE

  • Exceptional execution & delivery leadership: Proven experience as a delivery or execution lead, selecting outstanding talent and building highly collaborative teams in a fast-moving environment. You excel at translating complex R&D into operational reality.

  • A vision for modern control and data systems: Strong background working with safety and mission-critical software, combined with a vision to incorporate the best of modern software and AI into operational infrastructure.

  • Lessons learnt in high-consequence engineering: Proven experience in high-performance sectors operating under strict performance and reliability constraints. Demonstrated track record in critical external customer, vendor, and stakeholder management.

  • Operational and physical integration experience: You bring hands-on operational skills in mission control and real-time data analysis, combined with experience integrating software with physical hardware.

 

INTERVIEW PROCESS

  • Recruiter Interview (30-60 min)

  • Technical Screening (30 min)

  • Technical Panel (3x60 min)

  • CEO call (30 min)

 - Drive hardware R&D: Identify R&D opportunities for control and automation hardware. Act as an expert customer to specify and co-design with external vendors.

 -  Standardize clean interface boundaries: Establish hardware and software interface standards across subsystems. Collaborate closely with system teams that own edge-level hardware and software.
   
    

WHO YOU ARE

 - Exceptional execution & delivery leadership: Proven experience as a delivery or execution lead, selecting outstanding talent and building highly collaborative teams in a fast-moving environment. You excel at translating complex R&D into operational reality.

 - A vision for modern control and data systems: Strong background working with safety and mission-critical software, combined with a vision to incorporate the best of modern software and AI into operational infrastructure.

 - Lessons learnt in high-consequence engineering: Proven experience in high-performance sectors operating under strict performance and reliability constraints. Demonstrated track record in critical external customer, vendor, and stakeholder management.

 - Operational and physical integration experience: You bring hands-on operational skills in mission control and real-time data analysis, combined with experience integrating software with physical hardware.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
WHO WE ARE

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

BY JOINING OUR TEAM YOU’LL GET TO

  • Build the machine that builds the machine. Join TechOps at the forefront of advanced manufacturing, we’re building the production system that will enable commercial fusion. The Production lines, tooling, and processes are being developed from the ground up; you'll create the ways of working, not inherit them.

  • Work at the frontier of manufacturing technology. Bring your creativity to evaluate, qualify, and deploy processes with no industry playbook, every component you build and every process you shape goes directly into the core of the stellarator magnet technology.

  • Do work that matters, and see it grow. The hardware you build is the product and your career grows with it, from prototyping and process development through quality and industrialization, alongside exceptional colleagues from around the world.

  • Make an impact you can point to. In a small, fast-moving team, your calls on equipment, quality, and process directly shape how a world-class deep-tech company produces superconducting magnets with results visible on the shop floor, not buried in a slidedeck.

YOUR IMPACT

You keep Alpha's cost and schedule baselines honest against each other. Without a credible risk register and change process, changes slip into the program outside any controlled path, the IMS and cost forecast quietly drift apart, and a gate review surprises leadership with numbers nobody signed off on. Your job is to prevent that by making risk and change management a live, trusted function from the earliest stage of delivery, rather than something bolted on once problems have compounded.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

  • Establish and maintain the Alpha risk register across infrastructure, manufacturing and machine workstreams, facilitating structured risk identification, assessment and assignment of mitigation owners

  • Own the change control process end to end, from intake and schedule, cost and technical impact assessment through to approval routing and the change log, working closely with the Cost Controller and Programme Schedule Manager so all baselines reflect the same accepted changes

  • Prepare risk-adjusted inputs for release gate decisions, including quantified schedule and cost exposure and mitigation status

  • Run regular risk reviews with workstream owners and escalate emerging risks early, before they reach senior leadership as surprises

  • Build risk and change governance standards that scale as Alpha and Stellaris grow in parallel, with different partners and delivery models

  • Support the PMO's wider reporting cadence alongside the PMO Analyst/Coordinator


WHO YOU ARE

  • Experienced in risk and change management on major capital programs in energy, industrial, research infrastructure or similarly complex multi-discipline settings

  • Able to build a risk and change framework from scratch, not just administer an inherited one; you know what good governance looks like before it exists

  • Confident holding the line on change discipline with internal engineers and external partners who have their own priorities, combining analytical rigor with the communication skills to make it stick

  • Comfortable working with high autonomy while program structure is still being built

  • Fluent in English; German is a strong advantage given the contractor and regulatory landscape

  • Familiar with AI tools and digital ways of working, and quick to adapt in a lean, fast-paced environment

    INTERVIEW PROCESS

  • Recruiter Interview (30-60 min)

  • Technical Screening (30 min)

  • Technical Panel (3x60 min)

We know that diversity of thought and experience leads to better ideas, stronger execution, and a more resilient team. We don’t look at how you identify, what you look like, who you choose to worship or what ethnicity you are. We care about what you can bring to the table.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
WHO WE ARE

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

 

WHY JOIN PROXIMA FUSION

  • You will get to work on some of the most complex tech challenges to bring abundant, safe, clean energy to the world.

  • You'll get to join and learn from an exceptional selection of accomplished and driven individuals.

  • Do your life’s best work and enjoy the journey.

  • Get to show that big things are possible in Europe when you assemble the best talent.

 

YOUR IMPACT

At Proxima Fusion, we're developing the world's leading stellarator technology. To turn cutting-edge designs into reality, we need skilled technicians who can bring complex, first-of-a-kind hardware to life. As a Technician at Proxima Fusion, you'll work hands-on with Proxima-designed components, magnets, mechanical assemblies and other critical systems, supporting their build, assembly, integration and testing.

Working closely with Engineering, Manufacturing and Quality, you'll help turn ambitious designs into reliable hardware, solve practical challenges on the shop floor and contribute to developing the processes and tooling needed to build Alpha. This is a unique opportunity to work at the intersection of advanced engineering and hands-on manufacturing, helping build one of Europe's most ambitious engineering projects.

 

WHAT YOU WILL DO

  • Run acceptance and characterization tests across incoming High Temperature Superconducting (HTS) tape, cables, intermediate assemblies, complete plate assemblies, and completed coils, supporting both development and production.

  • Prepare and identify test articles by cutting, soldering, terminating, mounting, and fixturing in accordance with the test plan. Install sensors, voltage taps, feedthroughs and measurement wiring with careful grounding and shielding.

  • Set up and operate dimensional inspection equipment, electrical instruments, high-current supplies, liquid-nitrogen baths, cryostats, cryocooler-based rigs and vacuum systems after training and authorization.

  • Carry out critical-current and n-value measurements, joint-resistance, insulation-resistance and high-voltage insulation tests, plus visual and dimensional checks, using approved methods.

  • Configure data acquisition and check connections, signal quality and instrument settings before each run. Follow test sequences precisely, monitor sample behavior and pause or stop at defined limits or unexpected conditions.

  • Maintain full traceability of sample identity, test configuration, instrument settings, raw data, observations and deviations so that results and setups can be reproduced.

  • Check data for completeness and plausibility, reduce and present results clearly, and compare them with defined acceptance criteria. Record all deviations, escalate suspect results or failures, and obtain approval before changing acceptance criteria.

  • Troubleshoot test setups, wiring, instrumentation, and data acquisition. Distinguish test-article behavior from measurement faults, involving equipment technicians for machinery or rig repairs beyond approved routine care.

  • Keep rigs ready for testing through pre-use checks, calibration-status verification, approved routine care and consumables management. Coordinate servicing and calibration, and recheck the test configuration after maintenance.

  • Commission new fixtures with design and test engineering, and help turn development setups into documented, repeatable operations.

  • Support failure investigations through post-test inspection and, when authorized in an agreed investigation plan, sectioning and other destructive examination.

     

WHO YOU ARE

 

  • A technical apprenticeship or qualification in electronics, mechatronics, laboratory work or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.

  • Hands-on testing, laboratory or measurement experience in an industrial, research or engineering environment.

  • Practical electrical measurement skills.

  • The ability to read engineering drawings and wiring diagrams and work precisely to a formal test procedure.

  • Experience using data-acquisition systems and basic data reduction, with accurate record-keeping and the judgment to question implausible results.

  • A disciplined approach to safety, configuration control and traceability.

  • The ability to work across teams, communicate observations clearly and adapt as hardware and test methods develop.

  • Working English for following procedures, recording results and discussing technical findings.

  • Ln2 Experience

Nice to have

  • Experience with superconductoring, high or low temperature, cables or magnets, including critical-current measurements.

  • High-current DC testing or quench detection.

  • Experience with cryogenic testing, liquid nitrogen or helium, cryocoolers or vacuum systems.

  • Specialist low-level instrumentation experience, including voltage taps, feedthroughs, sensor mounting, grounding and shielding.

  • CAD literacy for reviewing or developing test fixtures.

  • Python or LabVIEW for test automation, data handling, and plotting.

  • German language skills.

 

INTERVIEW PROCESS

  • Recruiter Interview (30-60 min)

  • Technical Screening (30 min)

  • Technical Panel (3x60 min)

  • CEO call (30 min)

 

This job would require frequent travels to our office in Villigen ( Zurich, CH)

jobs.title: Scientist, Model Validation and Experimental Data Analysis
jobs.department: Stellarator Architecture, Plasma Modelling & Research, Numerical Optimization
jobs.team: Stellarator Architecture, Plasma Modelling & Research, Numerical Optimization
jobs.descriptionHtml:
WHO WE ARE

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.


TEAM AND ROLE

  • Shape the architecture of the world’s first commercial fusion power plant – Own system-level decisions that determine how a first-of-a-kind energy technology is designed, integrated, and ultimately deployed at scale.

  • Solve some of the most complex engineering challenges in industry – Work across tightly coupled disciplines (plasma physics, magnets, cryogenics, manufacturing, controls, and more) to resolve critical trade-offs and turn cutting-edge science into a functioning product.

  • Build real hardware with a pragmatic, fast-moving team from all over the world – Combine advanced simulation and systems thinking with a strong execution mindset, focusing on practical engineering solutions that accelerate the path to commercial fusion energy.

WHY JOIN PROXIMA FUSION

  • You will get to work on some of the most complex tech challenges to bring abundant, safe, clean energy to the world.

  • You'll get to join and learn from an exceptional selection of accomplished and driven individuals.

  • Do your life’s best work and enjoy the journey.

  • Get to show that big things are possible in Europe when you assemble the best talent.

YOUR IMPACT

You will make Proxima's plasma simulation stack trustworthy by confronting it with reality. Every prediction we make for Alpha – Proxima's Q>1 experimental stellarator – and for Stellaris, our commercial power plant, rests on models whose credibility has to be earned against real measurements from an operating device.

W7-X is where we earn it. You will take our integrated modeling framework, FUS3, and our Bayesian plasma state estimation workflow to W7-X data: reconstruct the plasma state from diagnostic measurements, compare our predictive models against what the machine actually did, and turn the discrepancies into a prioritized map of where our physics is right, where it is not, and what we must fix before Alpha's first plasma. Modeling sits on Alpha's operational critical path and cannot be backfilled after first plasma – this role is how we get ahead of it.

You will be the person in the group who lives at the intersection of modeling and experiment: fluent enough in the physics to know what a model should predict, and close enough to the diagnostics to know what the data can actually support.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

  • Validate Proxima's predictive plasma models against W7-X experimental data – neoclassical and turbulent transport, 3D equilibrium, ECRH deposition, pellet fueling and drift, bootstrap current and iota evolution – and record each comparison as a reproducible validation report with quantitative agreement metrics, stated limitations, and a pinned regression test

  • Reconstruct the plasma state from real diagnostic measurements using our time-dependent Bayesian state-estimation workflow (Thomson scattering, interferometry, CXRS, ECE, XICS, bolometry, magnetics), with calibrated uncertainties, and benchmark it against established analyses such as Minerva/IDA reconstructions and ASTRA power-balance results

  • Work with raw and pre-processed diagnostic data, not just analyzed profiles – instrument geometry, sightlines, calibrations and the caveats that come with them – and own the forward models, noise models and profile fits that feed transport analysis

  • Validate against databases of discharges rather than single shots, across W7-X magnetic configurations and operating regimes, so the output is a map of model applicability and parameter trends rather than one-off discrepancy reports

  • Act as a technical interface to W7-X and IPP: scope and prioritize data requests, spend time on site in Greifswald working alongside diagnosticians and operators, and propose and support experiments that directly target our model gaps

  • Feed validation back into design – convert diagnostic placement and observability studies on W7-X into requirements for Alpha's diagnostic set, and into realistic uncertainty models for the synthetic measurements we use to design against

  • Extend the modeling stack itself: mappers from experimental archives into IMAS, synthetic diagnostics, and analysis workflows, so that interpreting a shot end-to-end – raw data to reconstructed plasma state to physics quantities – runs in minutes and is reproducible by anyone in the group

  • As Alpha approaches operation, help stand up the between-shot analysis loop that will run on day one

WHO YOU ARE

  • PhD in plasma physics, fusion science, or a closely related discipline

  • Hands-on experience with experimental data from a magnetic confinement device – you have dealt with diagnostics, calibrations, systematic errors, and all the ways real data is messier than simulation output

  • Experience reconstructing the plasma state from measurements: profile fitting, integrated data analysis, equilibrium reconstruction, or power and particle balance analysis

  • Strong grounding in transport, equilibrium, and heating physics – enough to tell a code bug from a physics discovery

  • Rigorous about uncertainty; you treat a validation claim without error bars on both sides as incomplete

  • Comfortable writing and maintaining scientific software – version control, testing, and reproducibility are habits, not overhead

  • Can communicate effectively with physicists, diagnosticians, engineers, and experimentalists, and work productively inside an external collaboration

  • Self-directed; able to identify what needs to be done and execute

  • Willing to travel regularly to Greifswald, and later to the Alpha site

NICE TO HAVE

  • W7-X experience - operations, diagnostics, or data analysis, and familiarity with the W7-X data archive and Minerva

  • Stellarator physics background

  • Bayesian inference, uncertainty quantification, or machine learning applied to experimental data

  • Experience with integrated modeling and transport codes (FUSE, OMFIT, ASTRA, TRANSP, FUSE, JINTRAC, or similar) and with neoclassical (SFINCS, DKES, NEO) or gyrokinetic (GENE, CGYRO, GX, or similar) codes

  • Julia and Python programming – our integrated modeling framework is written in Julia

  • Familiarity with the IMAS data model

  • Familiarity with AI-assisted development tools

  • A track record of published validation studies or successful experimental proposals

INTERVIEW PROCESS

  • Recruiter Interview (30-60 min)

  • Technical Screening (30 min)

  • Technical Panel (3x60 min)

To get there, we need a high-performing, diverse team that brings different perspectives, challenges assumptions, and builds together with purpose. We know that diversity of thought and experience leads to better ideas, stronger execution, and a more resilient team. We don’t look at how you identify, what you look like, who you choose to worship or what ethnicity you are. We care about what you can bring to the table.

Modeling sits on Alpha's operational critical path and cannot be backfilled after first plasma – this role is how we get ahead of it.

You will be the person in the group who lives at the intersection of modeling and experiment: fluent enough in the physics to know what a model should predict, and close enough to the diagnostics to know what the data can actually support.



WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Validate Proxima's predictive plasma models against W7-X experimental data – neoclassical and turbulent transport, 3D equilibrium, ECRH deposition, pellet fueling and drift, bootstrap current and iota evolution – and record each comparison as a reproducible validation report with quantitative agreement metrics, stated limitations, and a pinned regression test

 - Reconstruct the plasma state from real diagnostic measurements using our time-dependent Bayesian state-estimation workflow (Thomson scattering, interferometry, CXRS, ECE, XICS, bolometry, magnetics), with calibrated uncertainties, and benchmark it against established analyses such as Minerva/IDA reconstructions and ASTRA power-balance results

 - Work with raw and pre-processed diagnostic data, not just analyzed profiles – instrument geometry, sightlines, calibrations and the caveats that come with them – and own the forward models, noise models and profile fits that feed transport analysis

 - Validate against databases of discharges rather than single shots, across W7-X magnetic configurations and operating regimes, so the output is a map of model applicability and parameter trends rather than one-off discrepancy reports

 - Act as a technical interface to W7-X and IPP: scope and prioritize data requests, spend time on site in Greifswald working alongside diagnosticians and operators, and propose and support experiments that directly target our model gaps

 - Feed validation back into design – convert diagnostic placement and observability studies on W7-X into requirements for Alpha's diagnostic set, and into realistic uncertainty models for the synthetic measurements we use to design against

 - Extend the modeling stack itself: mappers from experimental archives into IMAS, synthetic diagnostics, and analysis workflows, so that interpreting a shot end-to-end – raw data to reconstructed plasma state to physics quantities – runs in minutes and is reproducible by anyone in the group

 - As Alpha approaches operation, help stand up the between-shot analysis loop that will run on day one



WHO YOU ARE

 - PhD in plasma physics, fusion science, or a closely related discipline

 - Hands-on experience with experimental data from a magnetic confinement device – you have dealt with diagnostics, calibrations, systematic errors, and all the ways real data is messier than simulation output

 - Experience reconstructing the plasma state from measurements: profile fitting, integrated data analysis, equilibrium reconstruction, or power and particle balance analysis

 - Strong grounding in transport, equilibrium, and heating physics – enough to tell a code bug from a physics discovery

 - Rigorous about uncertainty; you treat a validation claim without error bars on both sides as incomplete

 - Comfortable writing and maintaining scientific software – version control, testing, and reproducibility are habits, not overhead

 - Can communicate effectively with physicists, diagnosticians, engineers, and experimentalists, and work productively inside an external collaboration

 - Self-directed; able to identify what needs to be done and execute

 - Willing to travel regularly to Greifswald, and later to the Alpha site

NICE TO HAVE 

 - W7-X experience -  operations, diagnostics, or data analysis, and familiarity with the W7-X data archive and Minerva

 - Stellarator physics background

 - Bayesian inference, uncertainty quantification, or machine learning applied to experimental data

 - Experience with integrated modeling and transport codes (FUSE, OMFIT, ASTRA, TRANSP, FUSE, JINTRAC, or similar) and with neoclassical (SFINCS, DKES, NEO) or gyrokinetic (GENE, CGYRO, GX, or similar) codes

 - Julia and Python programming – our integrated modeling framework is written in Julia

 - Familiarity with the IMAS data model

 - Familiarity with AI-assisted development tools

 - A track record of published validation studies or successful experimental proposals

INTERVIEW PROCESS

 - Recruiter Interview (30-60 min)

 - Technical Screening (30 min)

 - Technical Panel (3x60 min)

To get there, we need a high-performing, diverse team that brings different perspectives, challenges assumptions, and builds together with purpose. We know that diversity of thought and experience leads to better ideas, stronger execution, and a more resilient team. jobs.title: Integrated Electronics Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
WHO WE ARE

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

BY JOINING OUR TEAM YOU’LL GET TO

  • Architect a breakthrough energy technology – Play a defining role in designing and integrating the systems that will power the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion plant, influencing decisions that shape the future of clean energy.

  • Solve some of the most complex engineering challenges in fusion – Work across magnet design, HTS technology, manufacturing, structural integration, and controls, turning cutting-edge science into real hardware

  • Move fast and build what matters – Join a highly ambitious, multidisciplinary team that combines cutting-edge simulation with hands-on engineering, turning bold ideas into real hardware on the path to commercial fusion.

YOUR IMPACT

In this role, you will play a key part in developing the electronics that enable reliable and high-performance operation by translating functional requirements into robust electronic circuits, taking designs from initial concept and simulation through PCB implementation, laboratory testing, and integration into the complete converter. Your work will directly influence the performance, reliability, safety, maintainability, and will require close collaboration with power electronics, embedded software, mechanical, thermal, and system engineers.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

  • Design and develop PCB-based electronic circuits for converters, including gate drivers, auxiliary power supplies, sensing, signal conditioning, protection, and DC-link balancing circuits.

  • Define circuit architectures, select components, perform simulations, and develop schematics and PCB designs according to functional, electrical, thermal, and reliability requirements.

  • Explore novel circuit topologies, component technologies, and integration concepts to improve converter performance, efficiency, reliability, compactness, and functionality.

  • Build prototypes and perform laboratory testing, characterization, verification, troubleshooting, and validation of electronic circuits and PCB.

WHO YOU ARE

  • You hold a University (Higher education) degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, or a related field.

  • You are passionate about PCB design from concept through simulation, prototyping to production qualification.

  • You have owned electronic system design end-to-end through multiple rapid iteration cycles.

  • You are an expert in analog and digital electronics, including sensing, signal conditioning, power supplies, isolation, gate drivers, and optical interface circuits.

  • Experience with hardware-in-the-loop testing, automated test equipment, or laboratory test automation is a plus.

INTERVIEW PROCESS

  • Recruiter Interview (30-60 min)

  • Technical Screening (30 min)

  • Technical Panel (3x60 min)

We know that diversity of thought and experience leads to better ideas, stronger execution, and a more resilient team. We don’t look at how you identify, what you look like, who you choose to worship or what ethnicity you are. We care about what you can bring to the table.
